intro: A decision list, not a wish list. Each suggestion states what to do, why, what it costs, and what would make it a bad idea. Nothing here is implemented without a decision, except the rows marked shipped, which were built in this pass because the brief asked for them directly. The missing-information register below is the list of things worth finding out before the next decision is made.

statusKey.label: Shipped
statusKey.note: Already built on the live site in this pass.

statusKey.label: Recommend next
statusKey.note: Highest confidence, do this before the others.

statusKey.label: Consider
statusKey.note: Worth doing, but depends on an earlier decision.

statusKey.label: Hold
statusKey.note: Do not do this yet. Reason given.

statusKey.label: Rejected
statusKey.note: Would break a rule or mislead a reader.

suggestions.title: Keep the site in 'how to decide' voice, permanently, until products are actually tested
suggestions.why: The FTC forbids describing hands-on experience you do not have, and readers detect the fake version instantly. The reliable way to sound human without lying is to write about the decision instead of the verdict: what the drawers are like, what the counter cost is, who the machine is wrong for.
suggestions.cost: None. It is a writing constraint, enforced by the build.
suggestions.risk: A guide that never says 'we tested this' competes poorly against sites that can. That is a real disadvantage and it is the correct one to accept.
suggestions.decide: Accept. Every page already follows it.

suggestions.title: Split into two publications, or pick one category and go deep
suggestions.why: Three air fryers and two thermometers are two different buying moments. Search engines reward a site that owns one topic. A small site trying to own 'kitchen gear' owns nothing.
suggestions.cost: Splitting means two domains, two sitemaps, twice the setup. Going deep on air fryers means the thermometers get a single supporting page.
suggestions.risk: If the thermometer affiliate offers a better commission or a bounty, narrowing too early gives up real money.
suggestions.decide: Recommend: keep one site, make air fryers the front section, and treat thermometers as the accessory section — which is what the current structure already does. Confirm before adding a third category.

suggestions.title: Get PA-API or Creatives access before writing another word
suggestions.why: It is the unlock for the three things this site most obviously lacks: prices, ratings, and product images. All three are currently blank because the rules require API-sourced data. One credential fixes all of it at once.
suggestions.cost: Eligibility requires qualifying sales first — a chicken-and-egg problem for a new account.
suggestions.risk: None to the site. The risk is waiting on access and shipping nothing meanwhile, which is why the current build ships without it.
suggestions.decide: Apply as soon as the account qualifies. Track it in the questions register as Q-11 and Q-12.

suggestions.title: Replace the submitted short links with constructed Special Links and prove one works
suggestions.why: The submitted links carried no visible tag and their compliance status is unsettled. Constructing amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>?tag=shopnow047c-20 is unambiguous, keeps the destination visible in the status bar, and satisfies the link-clarity requirement.
suggestions.cost: None.
suggestions.risk: If the tag is not enrolled, every link still earns nothing. That is the one thing this cannot fix.
suggestions.decide: Already done. Next step is the proof: click one link per product while signed in, and confirm it appears in the tracking report.

suggestions.title: Publish on a real cadence: one guide a week for eight weeks, then read the query data
suggestions.why: Question-shaped guides are the right shape, but four is not a sample. A weekly cadence for two months produces enough pages and enough query impressions to see which question people actually arrive with, which is the only way to stop guessing topics.
suggestions.cost: One substantive guide per week. Each needs its own verified spec pass.
suggestions.risk: Cadence without quality control produces the thin content the brief explicitly rejects. The build gate must stay on.
suggestions.decide: Partly done, deliberately. Twelve guides now exist, but they were published in one pass, which is not a cadence. The weekly rhythm is still the plan, and the next topic should be chosen from the query report once one exists. Do not mistake a bigger library for a cadence.

suggestions.title: Add a real author byline with a named person
suggestions.why: Unattributed buying advice reads as generated, which is precisely the failure the brief names. A byline with a short bio and a stated method is the cheapest credibility signal available.
suggestions.cost: Requires a real person willing to be named and accountable.
suggestions.risk: A byline attached to content the person did not write is worse than no byline.
suggestions.decide: Decision needed from the requester. Cannot be fabricated.

suggestions.title: Move to a custom domain before building any authority
suggestions.why: A /WinA/ subpath reads as a side project, and moving later discards whatever equity accumulated. Doing it now costs a domain and one setting.
suggestions.cost: Domain registration plus DNS. About an hour.
suggestions.risk: Slight setup friction with HTTPS and the CNAME file.
suggestions.decide: Recommend. The build already keeps the origin in one config value, so the change is small.

suggestions.title: Deploy the analytics collector, and accept that orders cannot be counted yet
suggestions.why: Click data is available today and is the fastest honest feedback loop. Order data has to come from Associates reports, which arrive later. Separating the two keeps the ledger truthful.
suggestions.cost: One worker deploy and a secret.
suggestions.risk: A self-hosted collector is a privacy obligation. The current design stores no identifiers, which keeps that burden small.
suggestions.decide: Recommend deploying to close FLG-011. Do not import a third-party tracker as a shortcut.

suggestions.title: Add a 'who should not buy this' block to every product page
suggestions.why: The single most useful thing a buying guide can say, and the thing competitors skip. It also converts better, because readers trust a page that talked them out of something.
suggestions.cost: A short block per product.
suggestions.risk: None. It requires actually understanding the trade-off, which is why most sites omit it.
suggestions.decide: Shipped. Every product page carries a "Who it is wrong for" section, and the front page and the new /start-here/ page name the situation each product is wrong for rather than ranking it. Re-open this only if the site acquires a second authorial voice.

suggestions.title: Build a real comparison table with measured dimensions
suggestions.why: The comparison page exists but is thin because dimensions are unverified. Counter footprint is the number that actually decides a purchase, and nobody publishes it clearly.
suggestions.cost: Researching dimensions from manufacturer spec sheets, with a source link per number.
suggestions.risk: A wrong dimension is worse than a blank. Only add numbers with a source.
suggestions.decide: Consider once manufacturer sheets are gathered. Until then the table shows what is verified and says what is not.

suggestions.title: Add a short 'how we choose what to recommend' block to the front page
suggestions.why: Readers arriving cold need one sentence on why these five products and not others. It also pre-empts the 'is this an ad' reflex.
suggestions.cost: Three sentences.
suggestions.risk: Can tip into self-referential process talk, which the brief explicitly wants kept off the front page. Keep it to a single block low on the page.
suggestions.decide: Shipped. The front page carries a "How these recommendations were made" note, the front page strip shows the tested count as zero, and the /about/ page states the limitation. Keep it in the same place when the front page is redesigned.

suggestions.title: Do not add a price tracker, price alerts, or a deal feed
suggestions.why: Prohibited outright by §6(y) regardless of how it is built.
suggestions.cost: Zero.
suggestions.risk: It is the most requested feature on affiliate sites and the most direct route to account termination.
suggestions.decide: Rejected. Documented so no future session builds it.

suggestions.title: Do not generate volumes of near-duplicate pages to chase long-tail queries
suggestions.why: Template-spun variants of the same article are the definition of the thin, generated content the brief rejects, and they dilute the pages that could rank.
suggestions.cost: Zero.
suggestions.risk: It works briefly, then gets the whole domain discounted.
suggestions.decide: Rejected. The build gate refuses pages without unique content fields.

suggestions.title: Hold the email capture until there is something to send
suggestions.why: Collecting addresses with no ESP and no publishing cadence means collecting nothing. The form is currently inert and says so.
suggestions.cost: Saves an ESP subscription.
suggestions.risk: Capture opportunities are lost while waiting.
suggestions.decide: Hold until SUG-05 produces a cadence. Then wire one ESP and one welcome email.

suggestions.title: Hold all paid search
suggestions.why: No bid is permitted on Amazon marks, and a new site with no conversion data cannot tell whether an ad is profitable. Advertising before measurement is guessing with a budget.
suggestions.cost: Zero.
suggestions.risk: Slower initial traffic.
suggestions.decide: Hold until the ledger has real click and order data.

suggestions.title: Publish a dated 'last checked' line on every product page
suggestions.why: Specifications and availability change. A visible date tells the reader how much to trust the page, and forces the site to actually re-check.
suggestions.cost: One field, refreshed on a schedule.
suggestions.risk: A stale date is a public admission of neglect. That is the point.
suggestions.decide: Consider. Pages currently record the observation date in the register rather than on the page.

suggestions.title: Give every page a decision, not a summary: lead with the answer a reader came for
suggestions.why: The brief asks for a site that reads like a shop rather than an audit. The difference in practice is that a shop answers the question the customer walked in with, in the first screen, and shows the product next to the answer. This pass added a /start-here/ decision entry point, a seasonal layer at /season/, cluster grouping on the guides index, and a source list on every guide so a claim can be checked in one click.
suggestions.cost: None beyond writing.
suggestions.risk: A decision page can read as confident when it is not. Every answer on it points at a product shape and says what would make it wrong, and no page claims testing.
suggestions.decide: Shipped. Watch which entry points earn clicks once measurement exists; if /start-here/ is never entered, the answer is to link it more prominently rather than delete it.

suggestions.title: Ask each manufacturer for the interior cavity dimensions — the one figure nobody publishes
suggestions.why: Every capacity guide on this site currently ends in a gap: exterior dimensions are published, interior dimensions are not, and "can a whole chicken fit" cannot be answered from them. A single support email per model would close it, and it would close it for the reader too — this is the highest-value missing-information request on the site.
suggestions.cost: Three short emails and a week of waiting. Possibly a sample unit if they refuse to publish.
suggestions.risk: A manufacturer may publish a figure that does not match the unit actually sold, which is a different problem, not a reason not to ask. Record whatever they answer with its date and its source, exactly like every other specification.
suggestions.decide: Recommend. Do it before the next capacity guide is written, and record the answer in data/products.json with its source rather than in prose.

suggestions.title: Download the user guides for the three air fryers and record the care instructions
suggestions.why: "Dishwasher-safe" currently has to be treated as a claim because no official care instruction could be found for the nonstick baskets. The user guide is the document that settles how to wash them, and it also carries the interior cavity dimensions and the model number that distinguishes the 8-quart variants. One PDF per model answers three open rows at once.
suggestions.cost: An hour of downloading and reading.
suggestions.risk: Guides are model-specific and the 8-quart family spans several SKUs. Record which model number the guide belongs to and which ASIN it belongs to, separately.
suggestions.decide: Shipped for two of the three. The owner's manuals for the Emeril French Door AirFryer 360 (FAFO-001) and the ThermoMaven F1 Stealth (HT07) were downloaded and read in full, which closed the wattage, temperature-range, interior-volume, cleaning, calibration and probe-spec rows. chefman.com's published specification pages supplied the model numbers and the basket care instructions. The remaining gap is the basket fryers' interior cavity dimensions, which no published source carries.

suggestions.title: Ask ThermoMaven what the IP rating applies to — and to which part of the device
suggestions.why: Two official sources disagree in form. The Amazon listing title states "IP67 Waterproof"; the maker's own page says "100% waterproof" and publishes no IP number. The site currently shows both, attributed, which is honest but unsatisfying. One question to the manufacturer would settle whether IP67 covers the whole unit or only the sensing end.
suggestions.cost: One email.
suggestions.risk: Low. If they do not answer, the site keeps showing both statements, which is the correct fallback.
suggestions.decide: Shipped as far as it can be without the manufacturer replying. The maker's own user manual was read in full and publishes no IP number, so the specification row was downgraded from "verified" to "claim" and all three official wordings are shown. The row is only closable by a manufacturer reply.

suggestions.title: Ask Emeril Lagasse which preset count is current for this model
suggestions.why: The Amazon listing title for this ASIN says "24 One-Touch Preset Options"; the manufacturer's own specification panel says "25 Cooking Pre-sets". They may be counting different things (one-touch options against total pre-sets), but a reader is entitled to know which is which.
suggestions.cost: One email.
suggestions.risk: Low. Both statements stay on the site until the answer arrives.
suggestions.decide: Shipped. The owner's manual for model FAFO-001 contains a preset mode chart naming exactly 24 presets, which agrees with the Amazon listing title and disagrees with the maker's specification panel saying 25. The product page now leads with 24, states that the manual is where the number comes from, and shows the 25 alongside it. The accessory count has the same shape and is recorded the same way.

suggestions.title: Ask CHEF iQ how long the app and Smart Hub service will be supported
suggestions.why: The wireless thermometer is the one product on this site whose main feature depends on software. Nothing published states a support horizon, so the register records it as unverified rather than guessing. It is also the single most common complaint category for connected kitchen devices, and it is exactly the question a buyer should be asking before paying for it.
suggestions.cost: One email.
suggestions.risk: The honest answer might be "we do not commit to a date". That is still useful, and it is still publishable.
suggestions.decide: Still recommend, and now better evidenced. The full product page, its documentation links and its FAQ were read on 2026-11-20 and none states a support horizon. What is confirmed is that the probe and hub use internal rechargeable lithium batteries with no removable cells, so a probe depends on the hub as well as the app.

suggestions.title: Commission one hands-on test, properly disclosed, rather than guessing at everything
suggestions.why: This is the unlock the whole site is waiting on. Every guide currently ends at the edge of a measured fact: preheat time, how much a basket browns, whether the crumb tray is awkward, what the 450°F Hi-Fry burst actually does to a chicken wing. One tested unit per form factor would convert an honest inference site into an evidence site, and it would end the awkwardness of writing about an appliance nobody has ever switched on.
suggestions.cost: Three units, or one borrowed per category. Plus the discipline to write only what was measured.
suggestions.risk: Testing a single unit invites over-generalisation, and a disclosed test must be disclosed on every page that cites it. Both are manageable; neither is a reason not to test.
suggestions.decide: Recommend, and treat it as the real content strategy rather than a compliance nicety. Until it happens, the site stays in the "how to decide" voice, which is the correct voice for zero tests.

suggestions.title: Add a site search once there are more pages than a reader can hold in their head
suggestions.why: Thirty-nine pages is the point where a visitor arrives knowing they want "the chicken one" rather than a category, and a search box is the honest answer to that. It also concentrates internal linking on the pages that matter, which helps a small site more than another guide.
suggestions.cost: A generated index file and about forty lines of client-side JavaScript. No backend.
suggestions.risk: A client-side search over a static index is only as good as the index, and it cannot rank. It is a convenience feature, not a discovery strategy, and should not be confused with one.
suggestions.decide: Consider. Do it after the cadence in SUG-05 has produced a few more pages, so the index is worth searching.

suggestions.title: Do not publish year-stamped "best of" listicles
suggestions.why: This is the single most recognisable pattern of a generated affiliate site, and the brief explicitly asks for something that does not read like one. A "Best Air Fryers of 2026" list implies a tested, ranked, current verdict; this site has neither the tests nor the prices, and the year in the title guarantees decay. It also invites the copy-paste structure that every competitor publishes, which is not a strategy.
suggestions.cost: None. This is a prohibition, not a build.
suggestions.risk: The argument for it is that it is what ranks. It is what ranks in the short term, and it is what produces the pages that get penalised and abandoned.
suggestions.decide: Reject, permanently. Listed here so that a future session does not add one in good faith. The question-shaped guides are the deliberate alternative.

discovery.intro: Everything the site asserts is sourced. Everything the site cannot source is listed here, with the specific artefact that would close it and who can supply it. Nothing in this table is a guess; each row is a gap that was checked against an official source and not found.

rows.gap: Interior cavity dimensions for the two basket fryers
rows.why: Exterior dimensions are published; interior dimensions are not. "Can a whole chicken fit" and "does this feed four in one round" both reduce to this one number. The oven-style unit is now covered: its owner's manual gives the cavity as 26 quarts, 1519 cubic inches. The two basket fryers still have no published interior figure.
rows.close: For the oven-style unit this is closed — the manual gives 1519 cubic inches. For the basket fryers, one manufacturer support request per model, or the interior-dimension line in the user guide.
rows.effort: One email per basket-fryer model (two remain)

rows.gap: Care instructions for the basket fryers’ nonstick baskets
rows.why: chefman.com now states "Nonstick, dishwasher-safe baskets" for the 6-quart dual basket and "Top-rack dishwasher-safe basket" for the 8-quart, so the "dishwasher-safe" claim is now sourced to the manufacturer for both basket fryers. What is still missing is the care section of the user guide, which says how to wash them and what happens to the coating over time.
rows.close: The care section of the user guide for the exact model number.
rows.who: Manufacturer, or the listing's own care section on Amazon

rows.gap: Which dimensions and wattage apply to the 8-quart TurboFry
rows.why: The model is settled: the listing names RJ38-SQSS-8T and chefman.com publishes that same code. What remains is a value conflict — the listing states 12.75"D × 13.5"W × 10"H and 1000 W, while the maker states 15.4 × 12.6 × 13.5 in and 1700W. Both are on the page, attributed.
rows.close: A manufacturer reply naming the dimensions and wattage for the unit shipped under this ASIN.

rows.gap: What the IP rating on the ThermoMaven covers
rows.why: The Amazon listing title says "IP67 Waterproof"; the maker's page says "100% waterproof" and publishes no IP number; the maker's own user manual, read in full, publishes no IP rating either. The row is marked "claim" and carries all three wordings.
rows.close: A manufacturer statement of whether an IP rating exists and what it covers.

rows.gap: Whether the Emeril preset count is 24 or 25
rows.why: The owner's manual for model FAFO-001 has a preset mode chart naming 24 presets, which agrees with the Amazon listing title. The manufacturer's specification panel says 25 cooking pre-sets. The site leads with 24 and shows the 25 alongside it. The accessory count has the same shape of disagreement: six in the listing title, seven in the product description.
rows.close: A manufacturer reply naming the current preset and accessory counts.

rows.gap: How long the CHEF iQ app and Smart Hub service will be supported
rows.why: The product page, its documentation links and its FAQ were read in full and none states a support horizon. The probe and hub use internal rechargeable lithium batteries, so a probe also depends on the hub remaining serviceable.
rows.close: A manufacturer statement of the support horizon, and whether the device reports temperature without the app.

rows.gap: The intended ASIN for each of the five submitted short links
rows.why: The short codes were never ASINs and do not match the destinations. The observed ASIN is recorded; the intended one was never supplied and stays blank rather than being inferred.
rows.close: The requester stating, per submitted link, which product they meant.
rows.who: The requester — nobody else can supply this

rows.gap: Whether shopnow047c-20 is an enrolled Associates tracking ID
rows.why: Every link on this site carries it. If the account is not enrolled, nothing here earns anything and no amount of content fixes that.
rows.close: The Associates Central account page, or one live click test against the tracking report.
rows.who: The owner, in Associates Central — no access from here
rows.effort: One login, or one click and a 48-hour wait

rows.gap: Search Console impressions and queries for the published URLs
rows.why: Every guide title on this site is an editorial hypothesis. Nothing on it has been tested against what people actually type. Until the query report exists, topic choice is instinct.
rows.close: A verified Search Console property, then the Queries report after a few weeks of impressions.
rows.who: The owner, in Search Console — the placeholder token in every page head still has to be replaced

rows.why: Five events are defined and instrumented in the page script, but there is no endpoint, so nothing is recorded. No learning is happening.
rows.close: A host for the collector that is already written in _worker/collector.js, plus the endpoint written into the page config.
rows.who: The owner, or any host that will run a small worker
rows.effort: About an hour, once a host is chosen

rows.why: The Amazon listing title advertises a 450°F Hi-Fry option. The maker's own specification for the very model the listing names states 200–400°F and a 400°F maximum. The listing also calls it "4-in-1: Bake, Dehydrate, Frozen" where the maker says 4 cooking presets — two different things counted as four.
rows.close: A manufacturer reply stating the temperature ceiling for model RJ38-SQSS-8T and what its four functions are.

rows.gap: Whether the CHEF iQ probe has five internal sensors or four plus one ambient
rows.why: The same manufacturer page says both. The headline reads "Five internal sensors"; the feature list reads "4 internal temperature sensors for accuracy within 1°F" plus "1 ambient temperature sensor". The two readings imply different measurement hardware.
rows.close: A manufacturer reply stating the sensor count and what each sensor measures.
